items.stem: Which is the correct definition of displacement?
options: Total length of the path travelled
Distance moved in a specified direction
items.answer: Distance moved in a specified direction
items.markingKey: Displacement is a vector: distance in a stated direction from a reference point.

items.stem: Explain why an object moving at constant speed can still be accelerating.
items.answer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity; if the direction of motion changes (e.g. in a circle), the velocity changes even though the speed is constant.
items.markingKey: acceleration = rate of change of velocity [1]; direction change means velocity change [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between average speed and average velocity for a journey that returns to its starting point.
items.answer: Average speed = total distance/total time, which is non-zero; average velocity = displacement/time, which is zero because the displacement is zero.
items.markingKey: speed uses distance (non-zero) [1]; velocity uses displacement (zero) [1] [2]

items.stem: Sofia cycles 300 m due north in 100 s and then 350 m due east in 70 s. Calculate the average speed for the whole journey.
items.markingKey: (300 + 350)/(100 + 70) = 3.82 m s⁻¹. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: Lucas cycles 1200 m due north in 80 s and then 500 m due east in 90 s. Calculate the average speed and the magnitude of the average velocity for the whole journey.
items.answer: speed 10 m s⁻¹; velocity 7.65 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: total distance 1700 m ÷ 170 s = 10 m s⁻¹ [1]; displacement 1300 m [1]; velocity 7.65 m s⁻¹ [1] [3]

items.stem: A tram travels along a straight track at 15 m s⁻¹ for 10 s and then decelerates uniformly, stopping 5 s later. (a) Calculate the average speed for the whole motion. (b) Explain why the average speed is less than the initial speed. (c) State the difference between speed and velocity.
items.answer: (a) 12.5 m s⁻¹ (b) During braking the van moves more slowly than its initial speed, so the total distance per unit time is reduced. (c) Velocity is speed in a stated direction (a vector); speed is a scalar.
items.markingKey: (a) 188/15 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 12.5 m s⁻¹ with unit [1] [2] (b) During braking the van moves more slowly than its initial speed, so the total distance per unit time is reduced [1] (c) Velocity is speed in a stated direction (a vector); speed is a scalar [1]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of velocity?
items.answer: Rate of change of displacement
items.markingKey: v = Δs/Δt, a vector.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) What is 72 km h⁻¹ in m s⁻¹? (b) State the SI unit of acceleration.
items.answer: (a) 20 m s⁻¹ (b) m s⁻²

items.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards. Explain why its velocity at the top is zero but its acceleration is not.
items.answer: At the top the ball is momentarily at rest, so v = 0, but its velocity is still changing (from upwards to downwards) at 9.81 m s⁻² due to gravity.
items.markingKey: v = 0 momentarily [1]; velocity still changing, a = g downwards [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain what is meant by a negative acceleration when the velocity is positive.
items.answer: The acceleration is in the opposite direction to the velocity, so the object is slowing down (decelerating).
items.markingKey: acceleration opposite to velocity [1]; speed decreasing [1] [2]

items.stem: A car speedometer reads a steady 50 km h⁻¹ as the car travels around a roundabout. Explain whether the car is in equilibrium.
items.answer: No: its direction changes, so its velocity changes and it accelerates; a resultant force (towards the centre) acts, so it is not in equilibrium.
items.markingKey: velocity changing / accelerating [1]; resultant force so not in equilibrium [1] [2]

items.stem: Leila runs half-way round a circular track of radius 50 m in 40 s and claims: "My average velocity was 3.93 m s⁻¹." Identify the error and calculate the correct average velocity.
items.answer: Leila used the distance (πr = 157 m), which gives the average speed. Displacement is the diameter, 100 m, so average velocity = 2.5 m s⁻¹ across the track.
items.markingKey: used distance not displacement [1]; displacement = diameter [1]; correct value with direction [1] [3]

items.stem: Tariq walks 400 m due east in 150 s and then 150 m due west in 110 s. What is the average speed for the whole journey?
The speed of a motorcycle increases from 90 km h⁻¹ to 162 km h⁻¹ in 5.0 s. Calculate the average acceleration.
items.answer: 4.0 m s⁻²
items.markingKey: Δv = 72 km h⁻¹ = 20 m s⁻¹; a = Δv/t = 4.0 m s⁻². (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: Ines cycles 600 m due north in 120 s and then 150 m due east in 110 s. Determine the average speed for the whole journey.
items.markingKey: (600 + 150)/(120 + 110) = 3.26 m s⁻¹. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: The speed of a motorcycle increases uniformly from 72 km h⁻¹ to 126 km h⁻¹ in 4.0 s. Calculate (a) the acceleration in m s⁻² and (b) the distance travelled in this time.
items.markingKey: (a) convert: 20 and 35 m s⁻¹ [1]; a = Δv/t = 3.75 m s⁻² [1] (b) s = ½(u + v)t = 110 m [2] [4]

items.stem: Jonas cycles 450 m due north in 150 s and then 250 m due east in 90 s. Calculate the average speed and the magnitude of the average velocity for the whole journey.
items.answer: speed 2.92 m s⁻¹; velocity 2.14 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: total distance 700 m ÷ 240 s = 2.92 m s⁻¹ [1]; displacement 515 m [1]; velocity 2.14 m s⁻¹ [1] [3]

items.stem: A tram travels along a straight track at 15 m s⁻¹ for 20 s and then decelerates uniformly, stopping 5 s later. (a) Calculate the distance travelled at constant speed. (b) Calculate the average speed for the whole motion. (c) Explain why the average speed is less than the initial speed.
items.answer: (a) 300 m (b) 13.5 m s⁻¹ (c) During braking the van moves more slowly than its initial speed, so the total distance per unit time is reduced.
items.markingKey: (a) s = vt = 15 × 20: 300 m [1] (b) 338/25 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 13.5 m s⁻¹ with unit [1] [2] (c) During braking the van moves more slowly than its initial speed, so the total distance per unit time is reduced [1]

items.stem: A tram travels along a straight track at 12 m s⁻¹ for 12 s and then decelerates uniformly, stopping 5 s later. (a) Calculate the distance travelled at constant speed. (b) Calculate the deceleration. (c) Calculate the average speed for the whole motion. (d) State the difference between speed and velocity.
items.answer: (a) 144 m (b) 2.4 m s⁻² (c) 10.2 m s⁻¹ (d) Velocity is speed in a stated direction (a vector); speed is a scalar.
items.markingKey: (a) s = vt = 12 × 12: 144 m [1] (b) a = Δv/t = 12/5 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 2.4 m s⁻² with unit [1] [2] (c) 174/17 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 10.2 m s⁻¹ with unit [1] [2] (d) Velocity is speed in a stated direction (a vector); speed is a scalar [1]

items.stem: What does the gradient of a displacement-time graph represent?
items.answer: Velocity
items.markingKey: Gradient = Δs/Δt = velocity.

items.stem: Explain how a velocity-time graph shows a body moving with decreasing acceleration.
items.answer: The gradient (acceleration) decreases with time, so the line is a curve that becomes less steep (flattens out).
items.markingKey: gradient = acceleration [1]; curve becoming less steep [1] [2]

items.stem: A ball is dropped and bounces several times. Explain why its velocity-time graph has straight sections that are all parallel.
items.answer: Between bounces the only force is weight (ignoring air resistance), so acceleration is g every time; equal gradients give parallel lines.
items.markingKey: acceleration = g in flight [1]; gradient = acceleration so parallel [1] [2]

items.stem: A velocity-time graph for a delivery drone flying horizontally shows a straight line from (0, 0) to (5 s, 10 m s⁻¹), a horizontal line to (11 s, 10 m s⁻¹) and a straight line down to (14 s, 0). Calculate the total displacement.

A velocity-time graph for a lift moving upwards shows a straight line from (0, 0) to (4 s, 8 m s⁻¹), a horizontal line to (10 s, 8 m s⁻¹) and a straight line down to (15 s, 0). Calculate the deceleration in the final section and the average velocity for the whole journey.
items.answer: deceleration 1.6 m s⁻²; average velocity 5.6 m s⁻¹

items.stem: A velocity-time graph for a car in a test track shows a straight line from (0, 0) to (3 s, 6 m s⁻¹), a horizontal line to (11 s, 6 m s⁻¹) and a straight line down to (13 s, 0). (a) Calculate the acceleration in each section. (b) Calculate the total displacement. (c) Describe the shape of the corresponding displacement-time graph.
items.answer: (a) 2.0 m s⁻², 0, −3.0 m s⁻² (b) 63 m (c) curve of increasing gradient, then straight line, then curve of decreasing gradient levelling off at 63 m.
items.markingKey: (a) three gradients [2] (b) total area 63 m [1] (c) curve up / straight / curve flattening [2] [5]

items.stem: A lift starts from rest at the ground floor. It accelerates uniformly to 4.5 m s⁻¹ in 6 s, travels at constant velocity for 4 s and then decelerates uniformly to rest in 5 s. (a) Calculate the acceleration in the first stage. (b) Calculate the average velocity for the journey.
items.markingKey: (a) 4.5/6 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 0.75 m s⁻² with unit [1] [2] (b) 42.8/15 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 2.85 m s⁻¹ with unit [1] [2]

items.stem: A remote-controlled car accelerates uniformly from rest to 2.0 m s⁻¹ in 5 s, moves at this velocity for 4 s, then slows uniformly to rest in 4 s. (a) Calculate the acceleration in the first stage. (b) Calculate the total distance travelled.
items.markingKey: (a) 2.0/5 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 0.40 m s⁻² with unit [1] [2] (b) area of trapezium = 17 m (method/substitution) [1]; answer 17 m with unit [1] [2]

items.stem: What does the gradient of a velocity-time graph represent?
items.answer: Acceleration
items.markingKey: Gradient = Δv/Δt = acceleration.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) State how the acceleration at an instant is found from a curved velocity-time graph. (b) A displacement-time graph is a curve whose gradient increases with time. The object is …
items.answer: (a) Draw a tangent to the curve at that instant and find its gradient. (b) accelerating
items.markingKey: (a) tangent [1]; gradient of tangent [1] [2] (b) Increasing gradient means increasing velocity.

items.stem: Explain why the area under a speed-time graph gives distance but the area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement.
items.answer: Speed is always positive so all area adds as distance; velocity can be negative, so areas below the axis are subtracted, giving displacement.
items.markingKey: speed positive → distance [1]; negative velocity areas subtract → displacement [1] [2]

items.stem: Describe the displacement-time graph of a ball thrown vertically upwards and caught at the same height.
items.answer: A symmetrical curve (inverted parabola): displacement rises with decreasing gradient to a maximum (zero gradient at the top), then falls with increasing negative gradient to zero.
items.markingKey: parabolic/symmetrical [1]; gradient zero at top [1]; returns to zero [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain how to use a displacement-time graph to find the instantaneous velocity of an object that is accelerating.
items.answer: Draw a tangent to the curve at the chosen time; the gradient of the tangent (Δs/Δt using a large triangle) is the instantaneous velocity.
items.markingKey: tangent at the point [1]; gradient = velocity, large triangle [1] [2]

items.stem: A sprinter accelerates uniformly from rest; the v-t graph is a straight line from the origin. The final velocity is halved while the time taken stays the same. Explain how the distance travelled while accelerating from rest changes.
items.answer: The distance travelled while accelerating from rest halves.
items.markingKey: Using area under v-t graph = ½vt: distance travelled while accelerating from rest ∝ final velocity; factor = 0.500 = 0.500. 1 mark relationship, 1 mark conclusion.

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain how a velocity-time graph shows a body moving with decreasing acceleration. (b) A ball is dropped and bounces several times. Explain why its velocity-time graph has straight sections that are all parallel.
items.answer: (a) The gradient (acceleration) decreases with time, so the line is a curve that becomes less steep (flattens out). (b) Between bounces the only force is weight (ignoring air resistance), so acceleration is g every time; equal gradients give parallel lines.
items.markingKey: (a) gradient = acceleration [1]; curve becoming less steep [1] [2] (b) acceleration = g in flight [1]; gradient = acceleration so parallel [1] [2]

(b) Draw a tangent to the curve at the chosen time; the gradient of the tangent (Δs/Δt using a large triangle) is the instantaneous velocity.

items.stem: A velocity-time graph for a sprinter shows a straight line from (0, 0) to (6 s, 6 m s⁻¹), a horizontal line to (12 s, 6 m s⁻¹) and a straight line down to (17 s, 0). What is the acceleration in the first section?
items.answer: 1.0 m s⁻²
items.markingKey: gradient = 6/6 = 1.0 m s⁻².

items.stem: The displacement-time graph for Zara walking along a straight corridor is a straight line from (0, 0) to (5 s, 12.5 m), then a horizontal line until 10 s, then a straight line back to zero displacement taking 12.5 s. Work out the velocity during the first section.
items.answer: 2.5 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: gradient = 12.5/5 = 2.5 m s⁻¹. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: A trolley starts from rest and accelerates uniformly. Its displacement is 4.0 m at t = 4 s and 16 m at t = 8 s, and the displacement-time graph is a parabola through the origin. Explain why the gradient of the chord between these points gives the velocity at t = 6 s, and calculate this velocity.
items.answer: 3.0 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: for uniform acceleration the chord gradient equals the tangent gradient at the mid-time 6 s [1]; gradient = (16 − 4.0)/(8 − 4) [1]; = 3.0 m s⁻¹ [1] [3]

items.stem: A velocity-time graph for a car in a test track shows a straight line from (0, 0) to (2 s, 6 m s⁻¹), a horizontal line to (6 s, 6 m s⁻¹) and a straight line down to (10 s, 0). Calculate the total displacement.

The displacement-time graph for Mateo walking along a straight corridor is a straight line from (0, 0) to (5 s, 7.5 m), then a horizontal line until 8 s, then a straight line back to zero displacement taking 2.5 s. Calculate the velocity during the first section.
items.answer: 1.5 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: gradient = 7.5/5 = 1.5 m s⁻¹. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: The displacement-time graph for Freya walking along a straight corridor is a straight line from (0, 0) to (5 s, 25 m), then a horizontal line until 10 s, then a straight line back to zero displacement taking 25 s. Determine the velocity in each section and the average speed for the whole motion.
items.answer: 5.0 m s⁻¹, 0, −1.0 m s⁻¹; average speed 1.43 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: gradients: 5.0 m s⁻¹ and 0 [1]; return section negative: −1.0 m s⁻¹ [1]; total distance 50 m ÷ 35 s [1]; = 1.43 m s⁻¹ [1] [4]

items.stem: A trolley starts from rest and accelerates uniformly. Its displacement is 11.25 m at t = 3 s and 61.25 m at t = 7 s, and the displacement-time graph is a parabola through the origin. Explain why the gradient of the chord between these points gives the velocity at t = 5 s, and calculate this velocity.
items.markingKey: for uniform acceleration the chord gradient equals the tangent gradient at the mid-time 5 s [1]; gradient = (61.25 − 11.25)/(7 − 3) [1]; = 12.5 m s⁻¹ [1] [3]

items.stem: The displacement-time graph for Tomás walking along a straight corridor is a straight line from (0, 0) to (6 s, 18 m), then a horizontal line until 10 s, then a straight line back to zero displacement taking 6.0 s. Determine the velocity in each section and the average speed for the whole motion.
items.answer: 3.0 m s⁻¹, 0, −3.0 m s⁻¹; average speed 2.25 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: gradients: 3.0 m s⁻¹ and 0 [1]; return section negative: −3.0 m s⁻¹ [1]; total distance 36 m ÷ 16 s [1]; = 2.25 m s⁻¹ [1] [4]

items.stem: A lift starts from rest at the ground floor. It accelerates uniformly to 2.5 m s⁻¹ in 2 s, travels at constant velocity for 5 s and then decelerates uniformly to rest in 4 s. (a) Calculate the total distance travelled. (b) Calculate the average velocity for the journey.
items.markingKey: (a) area of trapezium = 20 m (method/substitution) [1]; answer 20 m with unit [1] [2] (b) 20/11 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 1.82 m s⁻¹ with unit [1] [2]

items.stem: A remote-controlled car accelerates uniformly from rest to 2.0 m s⁻¹ in 4 s, moves at this velocity for 4 s, then slows uniformly to rest in 5 s. (a) Calculate the acceleration in the first stage. (b) Calculate the average velocity for the journey.
items.markingKey: (a) 2.0/4 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 0.50 m s⁻² with unit [1] [2] (b) 17/13 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 1.31 m s⁻¹ with unit [1] [2]

items.stem: A lift starts from rest at the ground floor. It accelerates uniformly to 3.8 m s⁻¹ in 6 s, travels at constant velocity for 8 s and then decelerates uniformly to rest in 3 s. (a) Sketch the velocity-time graph, labelling key values. (b) Calculate the average velocity for the journey. (c) Describe how the displacement-time graph would show the constant-velocity stage.
items.answer: (a) straight line up to 3.8 m s⁻¹ at 6 s, horizontal to 14 s, straight line down to 0 at 17 s (b) 2.76 m s⁻¹ (c) A straight line with a constant positive gradient equal to the velocity.
items.markingKey: (a) three sections correct [1]; values labelled [1] [2] (b) 46.9/17 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 2.76 m s⁻¹ with unit [1] [2] (c) straight line [1]; gradient = velocity [1] [2]

items.stem: A steel ball is released from rest and falls a height h in time t. Which graph gives a straight line through the origin with gradient g/2?
items.answer: h against t²
items.markingKey: h = ½gt², so h ∝ t² with gradient g/2.

items.stem: Why is a small steel ball used rather than a table-tennis ball when measuring g?
options: Air resistance has a smaller effect on its motion
items.answer: Air resistance has a smaller effect on its motion
items.markingKey: A dense ball has a large weight compared with air resistance.

items.stem: Explain why plotting h against t² is better than calculating g from a single drop.
items.answer: A graph uses many readings, averages out random errors, reveals anomalous points and shows a systematic error as a non-zero intercept; g = 2 × gradient.
items.markingKey: uses many readings / reduces random error [1]; intercept reveals systematic error [1] [2]

items.stem: Chloe releases a steel ball from an electromagnet. An electronic timer records that it takes 0.492 s to fall 1.200 m onto a trapdoor. Calculate the value of g obtained.
items.markingKey: g = 2h/t² = 2 × 1.200/0.492² = 9.91 m s⁻². (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: A student measures the acceleration of free fall using an electromagnet, a steel ball, a trapdoor and an electronic timer. (a) Describe how the results can be plotted to find g more reliably. (b) State why a stopwatch operated by hand is unsuitable for this experiment.
items.answer: (a) Measure t for several h; plot h against t²; g = 2 × gradient. (b) The fall time is under half a second; reaction time (≈0.2 s) would be a large fraction of it.
items.markingKey: (a) several heights [1]; h vs t², g = 2 × gradient [1] [2] (b) The fall time is under half a second; reaction time (≈0.2 s) would be a large fraction of it [1]

items.stem: In a light-gate experiment, a card of length 5.0 cm passes through a gate in 0.020 s. What is its speed?
items.answer: 2.5 m s⁻¹

items.stem: A graph of h against t² for a falling ball has a positive intercept on the t² axis. Suggest a cause.
items.answer: The timer starts before the ball actually begins to fall (e.g. delay in release from the electromagnet), so every measured time is too long by a fixed amount.
items.markingKey: times systematically too long [1]; release delay cause [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the height should be measured from the bottom of the ball at release to the trapdoor.
items.answer: The ball travels this distance before it opens the trapdoor; measuring from its top or centre would give a systematically wrong h.
items.markingKey: distance actually fallen [1]; other points give systematic error [1] [2]

items.stem: Describe how two light gates can be used to determine g.
items.answer: Drop a card/interrupter of known length through two gates a measured distance h apart; find v₁ and v₂ from length/time at each gate; g = (v₂² − v₁²)/(2h).
items.markingKey: two gates and measured separation [1]; speeds from length ÷ time [1]; v² = u² + 2as rearranged [1] [3]

Tariq releases a steel ball from an electromagnet. An electronic timer records that it takes 0.492 s to fall 1.200 m onto a trapdoor. The uncertainty in h is ±0.002 m and in t is ±0.005 s. Calculate g and its absolute uncertainty.

items.answer: (a) 9.79 m s⁻² (b) The fall time is under half a second; reaction time (≈0.2 s) would be a large fraction of it.

items.stem: Amara plans an experiment in a practical class in Jakarta to determine g by dropping a steel ball through a measured height h and timing the fall. (a) Explain why the ball must be released from rest. (b) Describe how the results can be plotted to find g more reliably.
items.answer: (a) The equation h = ½gt² assumes u = 0; a non-zero initial velocity would give an incorrect (smaller) time. (b) Measure t for several h; plot h against t²; g = 2 × gradient.

items.stem: Lina plans an experiment in a school laboratory in Mumbai to determine g by dropping a steel ball through a measured height h and timing the fall. (c) State why a stopwatch operated by hand is unsuitable for this experiment.
items.answer: (a) The equation h = ½gt² assumes u = 0; a non-zero initial velocity would give an incorrect (smaller) time. (c) The fall time is under half a second; reaction time (≈0.2 s) would be a large fraction of it.

items.stem: A velocity-time graph for a car accelerating uniformly from rest is a straight line through the origin. The final velocity is reduced to one third while the time taken stays the same. State and explain how the distance travelled while accelerating from rest changes.
items.answer: The distance travelled while accelerating from rest becomes one third.
items.markingKey: Using area under v-t graph = ½vt: distance travelled while accelerating from rest ∝ final velocity; factor = 0.333 = 0.333. 1 mark relationship, 1 mark conclusion.

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why the area under a speed-time graph gives distance but the area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement. (b) Explain how to use a displacement-time graph to find the instantaneous velocity of an object that is accelerating.
items.answer: (a) Speed is always positive so all area adds as distance; velocity can be negative, so areas below the axis are subtracted, giving displacement. (b) Draw a tangent to the curve at the chosen time; the gradient of the tangent (Δs/Δt using a large triangle) is the instantaneous velocity.
items.markingKey: (a) speed positive → distance [1]; negative velocity areas subtract → displacement [1] [2] (b) tangent at the point [1]; gradient = velocity, large triangle [1] [2]

items.stem: A trolley starts from rest and accelerates uniformly. Its displacement is 25 m at t = 5 s and 49 m at t = 7 s, and the displacement-time graph is a parabola through the origin. Explain why the gradient of the chord between these points gives the velocity at t = 6 s, and calculate this velocity.
items.answer: 12 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: for uniform acceleration the chord gradient equals the tangent gradient at the mid-time 6 s [1]; gradient = (49 − 25)/(7 − 5) [1]; = 12 m s⁻¹ [1] [3]

items.stem: A velocity-time graph for a lift moving upwards shows a straight line from (0, 0) to (3 s, 8 m s⁻¹), a horizontal line to (11 s, 8 m s⁻¹) and a straight line down to (14 s, 0). Calculate the total displacement.

A velocity-time graph for a delivery drone flying horizontally shows a straight line from (0, 0) to (2 s, 18 m s⁻¹), a horizontal line to (12 s, 18 m s⁻¹) and a straight line down to (18 s, 0). Calculate the deceleration in the final section and the average velocity for the whole journey.
items.answer: deceleration 3.0 m s⁻²; average velocity 14 m s⁻¹

items.stem: A remote-controlled car accelerates uniformly from rest to 3.8 m s⁻¹ in 5 s, moves at this velocity for 10 s, then slows uniformly to rest in 5 s. (a) Calculate the acceleration in the first stage. (b) Explain how the graph would show the object later moving backwards.
items.answer: (a) 0.75 m s⁻² (b) The velocity would become negative: the line goes below the time axis and the area below the axis is subtracted from the displacement.
items.markingKey: (a) 3.8/5 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 0.75 m s⁻² with unit [1] [2] (b) line below axis [1]; negative area reduces displacement [1] [2]

items.stem: A lift starts from rest at the ground floor. It accelerates uniformly to 3.0 m s⁻¹ in 3 s, travels at constant velocity for 8 s and then decelerates uniformly to rest in 6 s. (a) Calculate the total distance travelled. (b) Explain how the graph would show the object later moving backwards.
items.answer: (a) 37.5 m (b) The velocity would become negative: the line goes below the time axis and the area below the axis is subtracted from the displacement.
items.markingKey: (a) area of trapezium = 37.5 m (method/substitution) [1]; answer 37.5 m with unit [1] [2] (b) line below axis [1]; negative area reduces displacement [1] [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) A ball falls from rest for 0.45 s. Taking g = 9.81 m s⁻², how far does it fall? (b) State one source of systematic error when timing a falling ball with an electromagnet release.
items.answer: (a) 0.99 m (b) Delay in the release of the ball as the magnetism decays (residual magnetism).
items.markingKey: (a) s = ½gt² = 0.5 × 9.81 × 0.45² = 0.99 m. (b) delay in release / residual magnetism / h measured to wrong point [1]

items.stem: Explain why a ball dropped from a large height gives a smaller value of g than one dropped from a small height, if timing is accurate.
items.answer: At larger speeds air resistance becomes significant, reducing the acceleration so the ball takes longer, giving a smaller calculated g.
items.markingKey: air resistance increases with speed [1]; acceleration less than g / longer time [1] [2]

items.stem: Sofia releases a steel ball from an electromagnet. An electronic timer records that it takes 0.454 s to fall 1.000 m onto a trapdoor. Work out the value of g obtained.
items.markingKey: g = 2h/t² = 2 × 1.000/0.454² = 9.70 m s⁻². (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: A card of length 2.0 cm falls vertically through two light gates 60.0 cm apart. The card takes 25.0 ms to pass the upper gate and 5.7 ms to pass the lower gate. Determine the acceleration of free fall.

A student measures the acceleration of free fall using an electromagnet, a steel ball, a trapdoor and an electronic timer. (a) For h = 1.000 m the time is 0.452 s. Calculate g. (b) Explain why the ball must be released from rest. (c) Suggest two reasons why the value of g obtained may differ from 9.81 m s⁻².
items.answer: (a) 9.79 m s⁻² (b) The equation h = ½gt² assumes u = 0; a non-zero initial velocity would give an incorrect (smaller) time. (c) Air resistance; delay in release from the electromagnet; error in measuring h (wrong reference point).
items.markingKey: (a) g = 2h/t² (method/substitution) [1]; answer 9.79 m s⁻² with unit [1] [2] (b) u = 0 assumed in h = ½gt² [1]; otherwise time too short/g wrong [1] [2] (c) first valid reason [1]; second valid reason [1] [2]

items.stem: A runner completes exactly one lap of a 400 m circular track in 80 s. What is the average velocity?
items.answer: 0 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: Displacement after one lap is zero, so average velocity is zero (average speed is 5 m s⁻¹).

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) A car speedometer reads a steady 50 km h⁻¹ as the car travels around a roundabout. Explain whether the car is in equilibrium. (b) Explain the difference between average speed and average velocity for a journey that returns to its starting point.
items.answer: (a) No: its direction changes, so its velocity changes and it accelerates; a resultant force (towards the centre) acts, so it is not in equilibrium. (b) Average speed = total distance/total time, which is non-zero; average velocity = displacement/time, which is zero because the displacement is zero.
items.markingKey: (a) velocity changing / accelerating [1]; resultant force so not in equilibrium [1] [2] (b) speed uses distance (non-zero) [1]; velocity uses displacement (zero) [1] [2]

items.stem: Aisha runs half-way round a circular track of radius 40 m in 30 s and claims: "My average velocity was 4.19 m s⁻¹." Identify the error and calculate the correct average velocity.
items.answer: Aisha used the distance (πr = 126 m), which gives the average speed. Displacement is the diameter, 80 m, so average velocity = 2.67 m s⁻¹ across the track.
items.markingKey: used distance not displacement [1]; displacement = diameter [1]; correct value with direction [1] [3]

items.stem: The speed of a motorcycle increases from 36 km h⁻¹ to 90 km h⁻¹ in 10 s. Work out the average acceleration.
items.answer: 1.5 m s⁻²
items.markingKey: Δv = 54 km h⁻¹ = 15 m s⁻¹; a = Δv/t = 1.5 m s⁻². (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: Freya cycles 1200 m due north in 80 s and then 500 m due east in 110 s. Determine the average speed for the whole journey.
items.markingKey: (1200 + 500)/(80 + 110) = 8.95 m s⁻¹. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [2]

items.stem: A tram travels along a straight track at 10 m s⁻¹ for 12 s and then decelerates uniformly, stopping 6 s later. (a) Calculate the distance travelled at constant speed. (b) Calculate the average speed for the whole motion. (c) State the difference between speed and velocity.
items.answer: (a) 120 m (b) 8.33 m s⁻¹ (c) Velocity is speed in a stated direction (a vector); speed is a scalar.
items.markingKey: (a) s = vt = 10 × 12: 120 m [1] (b) 150/18 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 8.33 m s⁻¹ with unit [1] [2] (c) Velocity is speed in a stated direction (a vector); speed is a scalar [1]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) A steel ball is released from rest and falls a height h in time t. Which graph gives a straight line through the origin with gradient g/2? (b) Why is a small steel ball used rather than a table-tennis ball when measuring g?
items.answer: (a) h against t² (b) Air resistance has a smaller effect on its motion
items.markingKey: (a) h = ½gt², so h ∝ t² with gradient g/2. (b) A dense ball has a large weight compared with air resistance.

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why plotting h against t² is better than calculating g from a single drop. (b) Describe how two light gates can be used to determine g.
items.answer: (a) A graph uses many readings, averages out random errors, reveals anomalous points and shows a systematic error as a non-zero intercept; g = 2 × gradient. (b) Drop a card/interrupter of known length through two gates a measured distance h apart; find v₁ and v₂ from length/time at each gate; g = (v₂² − v₁²)/(2h).
items.markingKey: (a) uses many readings / reduces random error [1]; intercept reveals systematic error [1] [2] (b) two gates and measured separation [1]; speeds from length ÷ time [1]; v² = u² + 2as rearranged [1] [3]
